questions.question: BK-499 scope after orientation. BK-485 constrains it: OP-01's D1 to D44 stay as they are, and a new step sits between record and spec. BK-397 constrains it: OP-01's dialogs are split across two logs (bcb85b21, f2ddab07), so a dialog check must read every log the trace lists. BK-496 is unrelated. What scope should this PR take?

options.label: BK-499 alone (Recommended)
options.description: Skill, axes, a new RFC amending RFC-0024 and any script or hook change. O14 to O26 stay undecided, BK-397's split-log remedy stays open, and the check reads every listed log as it is.

options.label: BK-499 plus BK-397's split-log remedy
options.description: Also fixes one session's log across two branches, so the dialog check reads one log per session. Wider PR, and it touches record_decision.py.

questions.question: Class 1 (C1, C2, G5): a consistency check is written once by the decision's author, names a subset of earlier decisions, and is never re-run. Which remedy? Whichever you pick, I'll run it on OP-01's record at c58ee74, untold, and it must find C1, C2 and G5 (ADR-0045).

options.label: End pass in session + unprimed reader after (Recommended)
options.description: Step 5 re-checks every decision against all others before Status Complete, with the maintainer there to answer. Then an unprimed agent reads only the record and ground in the step after, and its findings become open items. Two layers; the reader catches what the author is primed to skip.

options.label: Unprimed reader inside the session
options.description: The hook admits Agent in an armed session, so a reader confined to the same ground runs at End, and findings are asked before Complete. Needs a probe first: do subagent tool calls reach PreToolUse with the parent session_id? If not, the reader escapes the ground.

options.label: End pass in session only
options.description: Cheapest, with no new step. The same author re-reads, primed by its own dialogs, which is the failure ADR-0034 answers with an unprimed reader.

options.label: Unprimed reader after only
options.description: No skill growth at End. Every finding becomes a post-session open item that needs a reopen session, which is the cost this item exists to remove.

questions.question: Class 2 (O14 to O16): Decision text that no dialog asked (D35's read-phase list, E15 in D25, D19's table and its s4 sentence). The armed session cannot read sdd/decisions/, so any check runs after it. Can a script do it?

options.label: Script pairs, reader judges (Recommended)
options.description: Each Decision gains an 'Asked:' line quoting its question's opening words, or 'Settled by Dn'. A script pairs it with the answered dialog in every listed log. It fails on a missing or mismatched answer and prints Decision beside dialog. The class-1 reader judges text beyond the answer: a script cannot tell an elaboration from a new claim.

options.label: Reader with the logs, no script
options.description: The unprimed reader gets the record and the session's logs and pairs them itself. No format change and no script, but pairing 44 decisions by hand is where a reader skims.

options.label: Decision holds the answer only
options.description: The skill splits Decision into the answered option and a 'Derived:' bullet citing the decision each line follows from; a script checks the shape. Mechanical, but it checks form, not content (ADR-0045), and a session can still mislabel.

questions.question: Class 3 (C3 to C6): backend, SDK and runtime behaviour outside the unprimed ground. The remedy is a primed review step between record and spec, through a new RFC amending RFC-0024 D4 and the research § 9 step table. It writes open items to the record and never edits a decision. What is its ground?

options.label: Deps, platforms, vendors + src for feasibility (Recommended)
options.description: Dependency and SDK source, Python runtime and platform docs, and vendor docs; 0.33's src/ only as evidence of what a backend's SDK or OS does, never as the expected answer. That is audit-025's method, which found C3 to C6 and § 4.

options.label: Same without 0.33 src
options.description: No 0.33 code at all, so no 0.33 priming can reach a reopen. C3's evidence (Local's atomic write is os.replace) would come from the OS docs alone, and § 4's cost estimates would be lost.

options.label: Same, output as an audit doc
options.description: Ground as in the first option, but each run files an audit-NNN and the record only links it. More artifacts, and the record no longer holds its open items whole.

questions.question: Class 4 (C7, G1 to G4): the loop never asked these because no axis raises them: a caller's own deadline by cancellation (C7), the async stream's shape (G1), the file object's other methods (G2), an unknown encoding (G3), a failure re-raised as the same object or a new one (G4). axes.md is due for revision with F2 after the read() flow, which research § 9 puts before OP-02. When should the axes change?

options.label: Now: three generalized questions (Recommended)
options.description: AX-1 asks for every parameter and method that prior art gives a handed-out object, per form (G1 to G3). AX-6 asks what a resource in a failed state raises again (G4). AX-5 asks about a caller's own deadline and what it costs a handed-out resource (C7). A Sources line names audit-025. F2 still revisits the whole set later. OP-02 is covered even if F2 slips.

options.label: Now: one closing coverage sweep
options.description: No axis changes. The loop's last question becomes: every parameter, method and protocol a familiar prior-art equivalent has, each decided or open. Smaller diff, but a generic sweep is the kind of check a session ticks without asking.

options.label: Defer to the F2 revision
options.description: axes.md is unchanged; the five candidates go into BK-485's dossier for F2. Nothing enforces F2 landing before OP-02, so OP-02 may meet the same miss.

Class 1 missed your bar. Untold, on OP-01 at c58ee74, over three runs: reader run 1 found C1, the in-session End pass found G5, and reader run 2 found neither. No run found C2 (D39's adopted 'the next read resumes' vs D16); two runs judged it consistent, and audit-025 itself rates it optional, a note. Class 2 found O14 to O16 in both reader runs. What now?

options.label: Two readers, union, record the bound (Recommended)
options.description: /observe-review spawns two independent readers on the same brief and takes the union. That is the run-to-run variance seen here: run 1 had C1, run 2 did not. RFC and trace state the measured result honestly: C1 and G5 caught across the layers, C2 not, and why. No brief tuning on the test target.

options.label: Sharpen the brief generically, rerun
options.description: Add a rule such as 'for an adopted option, check each word about when or where (next, at open, only) against every earlier decision', then rerun all three untold. Might catch C2, but tuning on the test record risks fitting the brief to OP-01.

options.label: Ship as is, record the bound
options.description: One reader plus the End pass. RFC and trace state that one run caught C1, the End pass caught G5, and C2 went unfound. Cheapest; accepts the variance.

questions.question: The three runs also found OP-01 candidates outside audit-025. Recurring ones: D12 vs D28/D34 (E7 'connect never completes' gets timeout and unavailable); D22 vs D42 (a lost pin: changed or unavailable on SFTP); D9's adopted 'failure path only' vs D41's NP2; the Session's 'no decision cites a clause they check' vs D4/D9's KEY-001 and KEY-013. You said O14 to O26 are decided in a separate session. Where do these go?

options.label: Trace and PR only (Recommended)
options.description: Listed as evidence of what the check finds, unverified. The OP-01 record is untouched here. A later /observe-review OP-01 run verifies and files them, keeping this PR to the method.

options.label: Verify and file as O27 onward now
options.description: This PR re-reads each candidate and writes the ones that hold as open items in OP-01's record, as /observe-review would. Decisions stay untouched, but the PR grows and mixes method with record content.

options.label: File a backlog item

You said O14 to O26 are decided in a separate session. Where do these go?

questions.question: Accept RFC-0028 (sdd/rfcs/rfc-0028-observe-record-review.md)? It amends RFC-0024 D4 and the research flow. P1: /observe's End re-checks the whole record, and each decision gets an Asked line. P2: a review step between record and spec, /observe-review: a pairing script, two unprimed readers unioned, and a primed review against backends, SDKs and runtime. P3: the review only writes open items, never edits a decision. P4: three axis questions. Its Evidence table states C2 as a known miss.
